title: Independent-Cluster Replication of E21's Primary Confirmatory Condition
motivation: E21's 3,600-trial benchmark and its cell-specific bootstrap confidence intervals are correctly restricted, in the manuscript's own limitations section, to within-testbed repeated-trial uncertainty: all 3,600 trials ran against one kind cluster instance, one process environment, one long-lived proxy. This experiment replicates E21's primary confirmatory condition (idle load, sequential acquisition, all 3 conditions) on a GENUINELY SEPARATE kind cluster instance -- a fresh `kind create cluster` invocation, not a restart of the same container -- to test whether the core finding (DCJI issues fewer physical requests and completes commit-gate revalidation faster than FullRefresh, with 0 safety discordance) replicates outside the original single-cluster environment.
notes: Preregistered post-hoc extension (E26), run on a cluster and namespace entirely separate from E21's original cluster/data, which remain untouched. Scoped to the idle/sequential cells only (E21's primary confirmatory condition, per the original design decision recorded in that experiment's own materials) rather than the full 12-cell matrix, given this is a replication check rather than a new confirmatory benchmark in its own right. This is a genuinely new kind cluster instance (fresh 'kind create cluster', not a restart of flashir-e13), giving real cross-cluster (not merely cross-day) replication evidence.
